<section class="section s-white" aria-labelledby="what-title"><div class="wrap"><div class="head"><span class="eyebrow">A new pipe inside the old</span><h2 id="what-title">What pipe relining actually involves</h2><p class="lead">Four stages. The first one is the reason we will sometimes tell you the line cannot be relined at all.</p></div><div class="steps2"><div class="st2"><h3>The line is surveyed first</h3><p>Nothing can be relined until the inside of the pipe has been seen. The camera records the fault, its position and its length, and confirms the line still holds enough shape for a liner to pass through and sit against the wall.</p></div><div class="st2"><h3>The pipe is cleaned back</h3><p>A liner bonds to the pipe wall, so the wall has to be clean. mainEntity.name: How long does a relined pipe last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cured-in-place liners are a long-term structural repair rather than a patch, and the relined section no longer has the joints that failed in the first place. We do not publish a lifespan figure here, because the honest answer depends on the product used, the condition of the host pipe and the ground around it. You will be told what is being installed and what the manufacturer states for it before the work goes ahead.

mainEntity.name: Can any damaged pipe be relined?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and anyone who says otherwise has not looked. A liner needs a host pipe that still holds its shape well enough for the liner to be drawn through and pressed against the wall. Where a line has collapsed, dropped badly or lost its alignment, replacement of that section is the right answer. The camera footage is what decides it, and you see it.

mainEntity.name: Do you have to dig anything up at all?

acceptedAnswer.text: Relining itself is trenchless and is carried out through existing access points such as an inspection opening or a gully. In most jobs nothing is excavated. Occasionally a property has no usable access to the line at all, and a small opening has to be made to get to it. If that applies you would know before the work started, not afterwards.

mainEntity.name: How is relining different from just clearing the drain?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clearing removes what is blocking the line. Relining repairs the line itself. If roots keep coming back, clearing is treating the symptom: the roots return to the same crack or joint because the moisture is still escaping through it. Relining closes that opening, which is why it is the thing that actually stops the cycle.

mainEntity.name: Is relining cheaper than replacing the pipe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, but not always, and the comparison is rarely just the pipe. Replacement adds excavation, spoil removal and reinstating whatever was over the top, which is where the cost usually sits on a Sydney property. Where a line is accessible, shallow and in open ground, replacement can be the simpler job. Where it runs under a driveway, a slab or established garden, relining is usually both cheaper and far less disruptive.

mainEntity.name: Can you reline just one section?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A patch liner repairs a defined length rather than the whole run, which is the usual approach when the camera shows one bad joint in an otherwise sound line. Where a line has multiple faults along its length, lining the full run is often better value than repeating the setup several times.
